cases.title: Warriors–Trail Blazers: De'Anthony Melton free throw added after the game
cases.summary: The NBA reported that De'Anthony Melton's made first free throw was recorded as a miss. The final score was changed from Golden State 139–104 Portland to 140–104.

event.clock_precision: minute as stated by NBA.com / NBC Sports Bay Area
event.play: Melton made the first of two free throws; the NBA account says the in-game statisticians recorded both attempts as misses.

immediately_after_original_entry.derivation: The official NBA.com account says both free throws were recorded as missed; that entry adds no points to the reported 91–67 score before the trip.

immediately_after_corrected_entry.derivation: One made free throw adds one point to Golden State's source-reported 91–67 score before the trip. This is a transparent calculation, not a separately preserved scoreboard snapshot.

scores.total_calculation_note: Totals are arithmetic sums of the listed team scores; the NBA report states the team-score change directly.

player_points.note: The exact corrected official Melton player total remains unresolved: NBC Sports Bay Area and ESPN show 11, while FanSided reports 12. No corrected official NBA player-line snapshot was recovered. The team-score correction is confirmed; neither player total is promoted to an NBA-verified value.

source_observations.observation: NBA.com reports the initial 139–104 final, the corrected 140–104 final, and the missed-make error at 2:00 of the third quarter.
source_observations.timestamp_precision: date; NBA.com page separately labels an update time without a timezone
source_observations.role: NBA.com publication carrying an Associated Press report

source_observations.observation: NBC Sports Bay Area reports that Golden State led 91–67 when Melton first attempted the free throws, and that the score was updated to 140–104.
source_observations.role: Independent reporting for the event-local score

source_observations.timestamp_precision: second, UTC; announcement time, not verified database-update time

source_observations.observation: The ESPN page reviewed after the correction showed a 140–104 final and Melton with 11 points and 1-for-2 free throws. This is a current secondary page, not a preserved original NBA box-score snapshot.
source_observations.timestamp_precision: date of review; page publication/update time not established
source_observations.role: current secondary box-score observation; one position in the unresolved player-line disagreement

source_observations.observation: The ESPN score table showed 140–104 while the embedded Associated Press narrative retained 139–104. These are inconsistent components on one provider page, not evidence of a second NBA correction.
source_observations.timestamp_precision: date of review; not a preserved game-night page capture

source_observations.observation: The CBS GameTracker page reviewed showed a 139–104 score and a 10-point / 0-for-2 Melton line, while embedded AP copy said 140–104. The page-component update history is unknown; this is retained as a secondary-provider inconsistency, not an NBA-record correction.
source_observations.timestamp_precision: date of review; not a preserved game-night page capture
source_observations.role: secondary-provider internal inconsistency; component update history unknown

source_observations.observation: FanSided reports that Melton’s player total changed from 11 to 12 after the correction. This conflicts with the 11-point values reported by NBC Sports Bay Area and shown on ESPN’s current box-score page; no corrected official NBA player-line snapshot was recovered.
source_observations.timestamp_precision: date of secondary report review; report publication date is not treated as a database-update timestamp
source_observations.role: secondary report of the conflicting 12-point position

timeline.event: Game played; the NBA's later account identifies 139–104 as the score before correction.

timeline.timestamp_precision: second, UTC for the NBA Official post only
timeline.event: NBA.com reported the error and the corrected 140–104 final; the official account post is timestamped at this time.

cause.description: The NBA.com report says game statisticians recorded both of Melton's free throws as missed even though he made the first. The cause is therefore a scorekeeping entry error; a more specific operational cause is not stated.

duration.note: The official announcement has a timestamp, but the exact time the initial final score first appeared is not established by the reviewed sources. Correction duration is not calculated.

unknowns: The exact first-publication time of the original final score is not established.
The exact time the NBA's underlying score record changed is not established; the NBA Official post time is only an announcement timestamp.
The exact corrected official Melton player total remains unresolved: NBC Sports Bay Area and ESPN show 11, while FanSided reports 12; no corrected official NBA player-line snapshot was recovered.

cases.title: Cavaliers–Wizards: Tre Johnson free throw added the next day
cases.summary: The initial reported final was Cleveland 148–114 Washington. On the following day the NBA announced that a Tre Johnson free throw entered as a miss was made, and the corrected final became 148–115.

event.clock_precision: minute as quoted in the reported NBA statement
event.play: The NBA statement, as quoted by The Athletic, says Johnson's first free throw was entered as missed although he made it; the report says he was credited with no point for that first make on the live scoreboard.

immediately_after_corrected_entry.derivation: The source reports a made Washington free throw and a 50–39 score before the attempt. A made free throw adds one point; no separate corrected in-game scoreboard capture was located.

scores.total_calculation_note: Totals are arithmetic sums of the listed team scores. The NBA Gamebook records Cleveland 148 and Washington 115; The Athletic reports that the NBA corrected the score the next day.

player_points.originally_reported_note: No contemporaneously timestamped source preserving Johnson’s pre-correction player total was verified. CBS Sports’ page reviewed in 2026-10-07 shows 18 in a separate stale-looking stat component, but its original publication/update time is unknown; it is not asserted as the game-night value.

source_observations.observation: The Associated Press recap displayed by ESPN on game night reported Cleveland 148–114 Washington. It does not independently preserve a Tre Johnson player total.
source_observations.timestamp_precision: minute as displayed by ESPN; timezone not supplied
source_observations.role: game-night secondary report of the original final

source_observations.observation: The Athletic reports that the NBA acknowledged on the following morning that Johnson made both free throws at Q2 8:15, that the first attempt had been entered as a miss, and that the final changed from 148–114 to 148–115. It also reports Johnson was updated from 18 to 19 points and attributes a human-error explanation to a league operations executive.
source_observations.timestamp_precision: date for the report; exact score-update time not established
source_observations.role: secondary reporting quoting the NBA correction statement and a league operations executive

source_observations.observation: NBA Official’s post states that Tre Johnson’s first free throw at 8:15 of Q2 was incorrectly entered as missed even though he made both, and that game statistics were corrected. The post does not preserve the original live box-score state or the exact time the underlying record changed.
source_observations.timestamp_precision: minute, UTC as retained from the official post ID; seconds not claimed; announcement time, not database-update time
source_observations.role: primary league announcement of the correction

source_observations.observation: On review dated 2026-10-07, the ESPN game page header showed 148–115 while its embedded AP recap still showed 148–114.
source_observations.timestamp_precision: date of review; current page-component comparison, not a preserved game-night page capture

source_observations.observation: The current NBA game summary lists the final linescore as Cleveland 148 and Washington 115.
source_observations.timestamp_precision: date of review; current page, not an archived pre-correction snapshot

source_observations.observation: The official NBA Gamebook records a 148–115 final and lists Tre Johnson with 19 points and Washington at 18-for-23 from the free-throw line. It corroborates the corrected final/player total, but does not preserve the original live score or the error explanation.
source_observations.timestamp_precision: date of review of the official gamebook for the 2025-11-07 game
source_observations.role: official box score and gamebook for the corrected final/player total

source_observations.observation: CBS Sports’ current recap headline and article text report the corrected 148–115 final, state that the NBA added a point after the game, and give Johnson 19 points.
source_observations.timestamp_precision: date of review; recap itself is dated 2025-11-08

source_observations.observation: On the page reviewed 2026-10-07, CBS Sports’ boxscore header and quarter-by-quarter total show 148–115, but its Team Stats table lists Washington at 114 and its Tre Johnson row lists 18 points. Its Q2 8:15 play-by-play labels Johnson’s first free throw missed, then the second made, ending that sequence at 50–40. These retained components conflict with the reported NBA correction and the corrected recap on the same page; their update path and timing are unknown.
source_observations.timestamp_precision: date of review; current secondary-page components, not a preserved game-night page capture
source_observations.role: later secondary-page internal inconsistency; not evidence identifying which party caused the original error

timeline.timestamp_precision: minute as displayed by ESPN, timezone not supplied; initial-report display time, not an NBA database timestamp
timeline.event: Game-night reporting recorded Cleveland 148–114 Washington. A contemporaneous original player total for Tre Johnson was not established from the reviewed recap.

timeline.timestamp_precision: minute, UTC from the NBA Official post; announcement timestamp only, not exact underlying score-update time
timeline.event: The NBA announced a correction; the final changed to 148–115 and Johnson’s line to 19 points.
Current ESPN and CBS pages were reviewed. Corrected and stale components coexist; CBS’s historical play-by-play and team/player stat components still show the earlier values.

cause.description: The NBA statement quoted by The Athletic says the made free throw was entered as missed. A league operations executive separately described the scorekeeping miss as human error and said a full-game review caught it; this detail is attributed to The Athletic's interview, not an independently retrieved NBA document.

duration.note: The correction was announced the day after the game, but the exact initial-display and database-update timestamps are not established. No duration is inferred.

unknowns: The exact timestamp when the corrected NBA score first appeared is not established.
The complete corrected score immediately after both free throws was not independently archived; event-local values shown here concern the first attempt only.

The Athletic article may be access-restricted for some readers. The official NBA Gamebook independently corroborates the corrected final and Johnson’s 19-point total, but does not preserve the original live snapshot or the correction explanation.

The relationship between CBS Sports’ retained Q2 play-by-play/stat components and the original NBA scoring entry is not established; the current page does not show when those components were last updated.
No contemporaneously timestamped original Tre Johnson player total was verified. The CBS Sports component showing 18 was observed in 2026, and its update history is unknown.
